The line y=x+k meets OA at U=(-k,0) and AB (y=-4x+16) at V. The triangle cut off at A has area 1/2·(4+k)·4(4+k)/5=2(4+k)^2/5. Setting this to half the full area 4 gives (4+k)^2=10. The shown intersection is on the relevant side, so at x=4, a=4+k=√10 and a²=10.

Use affine coordinates B=(0,0), C=(1,0), A=(0,1). External division gives E=(-2,0) for BE:EC=2:3 and F=(0,2) for AF:FB=1:2. Triangle FEC has base EC=3 and height 2, area 3; ABC area is 1/2. Ratio k=6.

At x=i, consecutive odd-power factors pair as (1+i)(1-i)=2. For even n, the product is 2^(n/2); for odd n it has a nonzero imaginary factor (1+i). Divisibility by x²+1 requires the product at i to equal 128=2^7, so n=14.

The roots are 2a and a²-2a, so interval length is |a(4-a)|. An integer-length interval has exactly four integers when length 3 with an integer endpoint, or length 4 with noninteger endpoints. For length 3, a=1,3 qualify (their endpoints are integers); the exterior roots 2±√7 have noninteger endpoints and only three integers. For length 4, a=2 has integer endpoints and five integers, while a=2±2√2 have noninteger endpoints and four integers. The qualifying sum is 1+3+(2+2√2)+(2-2√2)=8.

The cubic factors as (x-1)(x²+ax+a). A repeated root occurs if the quadratic discriminant a(a-4)=0 (a=0,4), or if the quadratic also has root 1, 1+2a=0 (a=-1/2). Each gives a double root and a distinct other real root. Sum=0+4-1/2=7/2.
AB has slope -1/2, so the altitude from O is y=2x. OB has slope -3, so the altitude from A has slope 1/3: y-3=(x-4)/3. Their intersection is P=(1,2). The area is |det((4,3),(1,2))|/2=5/2.
